title: Request fingerprinting + per-tenant leaky-bucket to reduce 5xx cascades and noisy retries
text:
Request fingerprinting + per-tenant leaky-bucket to reduce 5xx cascades and noisy retries

description:
Summary: Multiple customers escalated production-visible spikes of 5xx and timeouts during short tenant bursts. Investigation shows a combination of client retries + upstream transient errors + request fanout that produced amplified load on model serving. Proposed fix introduces a lightweight request fingerprint at the proxy + a per-tenant leaky-bucket admission controller to suppress retry storms and provide caller-aware fast-fail semantics. The approach is intentionally minimal and reversible: (1) fingerprint to deduplicate in-flight idempotent requests and label bursts, (2) per-tenant leaky bucket to cap ingress rate and shape retries, (3) caller-aware fast-fail path that returns 429/503 earlier for overloaded tenants rather than letting requests reach the GPU layer and cause cascading KV/cache churn. This ticket covers design, implementation in edge-proxy and routing, observability, rollout, and customer communication.

acceptance_criteria:
Proxy attaches a deterministic fingerprint header for eligible requests (POST /v1/generate and streaming) and fingerprint is visible in traces
Edge rejects > configured tenant burst window with 503 or 429 before forwarding to model-serving for >90% of synthetic overload tests
End-to-end integration test that replays a customer surge + client retries shows at least 4x reduction in model-serving request rate compared to current behavior
No regression in latency for non-burst normal traffic (95th percentile change < 5%)
Dashboard added: tenant burst rate, dedup hits, fast-fail rate, downstream 5xx delta (pre/post)

deployment_plan:
Phased rollout across edge clusters: 1) Canary in region-us-east-1 (5% edge traffic) with feature flag off by default for managed tenants, 2) Enable fingerprinting-only for all tenants (2 days) to collect telemetry, 3) Turn on leaky-bucket in soft mode (drop with 429) for low-risk tenants (10% traffic) and monitor for 48h, 4) Gradually expand to all hosted tenants. Each step gated by automated SLO checks (error_budget_remaining > 60% and downstream 5xx trend stable).

rollback_plan:
Feature flag at proxy level to disable leaky-bucket + fingerprint. If downstream latency or error rate regresses beyond thresholds, flip flag in canary and roll back to fingerprint-only. If widespread issue, disable fingerprint header across edges to return to current behavior. Emergency playbook: follow RUNBOOK-ESCL-1 to revert within 15 minutes.

monitoring_and_alerting:
Create dedicated Grafana panel and alerts: (A) tenant_fastfail_rate > 2% for more than 15m -> P1 alert, (B) dedup_hit_ratio < 0.01 when expected >0.1 -> investigate fingerprinting bug, (C) downstream_5xx_drop_rate not improving after rollout -> Pager to SRE. Add log sampling for fingerprint mismatches and link traces to honeycomb (trace tag: req.fingerprint).

notes:
Design trade-offs: we considered global request deduplication via centralized cache but rejected due to latency and operational complexity; per-proxy deterministic fingerprint is weaker but simpler and sufficient for majority of retry storms.
Fingerprint composition: sha1(client-id + api-key-suffix + request-path + body-prefix(256) + timestamp-bucket). This produces stable dedupe within a short window and respects payload privacy (we don't log full body).
Leaky-bucket params: default capacity=20 reqs/60s, refill=1req/3s per tenant; will be tunable per-tenant. Values chosen after load testing against historical burst traces.
Fallback semantics: non-idempotent endpoints continue to bypass dedupe but still subject to leaky-bucket admission.

comments:
2025-02-18 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after SOC call with CS; attached initial investigation notes and sample traces (confluence: /spaces/HOSTED/retry-storm-analysis).
2025-02-19 Miguel Torres: POC complete for fingerprint header and simple dedupe counter in proxy. Local load test shows 3.6x reduction in forwarded requests for retry patterns. PR opened (edge-proxy#1327).
2025-02-20 Keisha Wong (SRE): Observability hooks added; requested an extra metric for 'dedup_drop_reason' to differentiate hash collisions vs ineligible requests.
2025-02-21 Product (Liam O'Connor): Customer comm draft ready for Acme and LogiAI; propose notifying customers when their tenant is in soft-leaky mode and provide guidance to adjust client retry backoff.
2025-02-23 Miguel Torres: Canary test started in us-east-1 with fingerprint-only. Early telemetry: dedup_hit_ratio=0.12 on synthetic burst. No notable latency regressions. Moving to soft leaky-bucket for 10% of traffic tomorrow.
2025-02-24 SRE on-call (Keisha Wong): After enabling soft leaky-bucket, model-serving request rate dropped 4.2x for the burst scenario; downstream 5xxs decreased by ~72% in canary. Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted. Noted one client reported increased 429s; CS notified.
2025-02-25 Miguel Torres: Rolling to 25% edge traffic. Added integration test in CI to simulate jittered client retries and assert dedupe behavior. Next: add per-tenant config UI in Console for opt-out and thresholds (tracked in PM-402).
